bugs.summary: methods() works, showMethods() fails for S4 methods loaded but not attached
bugs.creator: maechler

comments.creator: maechler
comments.text:
A repr.ex. is easiest with the `Matrix` package. (as that is present everywhere):

```r
> str(Matrix::rankMatrix)
function (x, tol = NULL, method = c("tolNorm2", "qr.R", "qrLINPACK", "qr", 
    "useGrad", "maybeGrad"), sval = svd(x, 0, 0)$d, warn.t = TRUE)  
> methods("qr")
[1] qr,ANY-method          qr,dgCMatrix-method    qr,sparseMatrix-method
[4] qr.default             qr.lm*                
see '?methods' for accessing help and source code
> showMethods("qr")

Function "qr":
 <not an S4 generic function>
> showMethods(qr)

Function "qr":
 <not an S4 generic function>
> .S4methods("qr")
[1] qr,sparseMatrix-method qr,dgCMatrix-method    qr,ANY-method         
see '?methods' for accessing help and source code
> 
> showMethods(Matrix::qr)  ## this does work (but is "not obvious")
Function: qr (package base)
x="ANY"
x="dgCMatrix"
x="matrix"
    (inherited from: x="ANY")
x="sparseMatrix"

> 
```

Also note that `?methods` (the help page) talks about finding methods in packages in the search path, but not about finding methods in non-attached namespaces.

Relatedly,  `selectMethod()`  in this situation finds the S4 methods well,
but it seems,  they are  *not*  selected in reality.

Last but not least: Maybe this *is* special because 'qr' is from base and hence cannot be imported into Matrix before it is augmented with S4 methods there and then these are (re)exported via   `exportMethods("qr")`

reproducible ex. script ('short_showMethods...')

comments.text:
Package **methods** is not consistent about where it looks for generic function definitions, by its own admission, e.g., `help("getMethod")` says:

> In contrast, `findMethod` has a different default and the optional `where=` argument may be needed.

Called without `where=`, `findMethod` and `showMethods` use `getGeneric(f, where = where)`.  The default expression for `where` evaluates to `.GlobalEnv`, so only attached package environments are searched.

Called without `where=`, `getMethod` and `selectMethod` use `getGeneric(f)`, so the cache `methods:::.genericTable` is searched first.  `.S4methods` (called from `methods`) also uses `getGeneric(f)`.

It would be nice to make consistent the default behaviours of these functions admitting a formal argument `where`.  If we do that, then my preference would be to give more information rather than less, hence to in more places consult the cache when `where` is missing from the call.

(In reply to Mikael Jagan from comment #4)

comments.text:
(In reply to Martin Maechler from comment #5)
> (In reply to Mikael Jagan from comment #4)

.. Ah, now of course, it is more complicated and I think we need a more sophisticated solution (than what the above comment #4 (and #5) implied) :

I maintain we must consider (for the default behaviour) which *was* on my mind when reporting this as a bug:

Both `methods()` and `showMethods()` should show the methods that *are* used, i.e., dispatched to when the user calls `<generic>(<some class>, ..)`.
Coming back to my Matrix package example, this would currently *not* dispatch
to the sparseMatrix-methods when Matrix is only loaded but not in the `search()` path... *unless* one uses  `Matrix::<generic>(<some class>, ..)`,
see the very end of my repro.R script (attachment 2667 from July 2020):
```
        qr(tsM) # -> dense and base::qr()
Matrix::qr(tsM) # -> sparseQR
```

I still agree and think we should make  `methods()` and `showMethods()` more compatible, and maybe by a version of the following idea:

For a long time now {almost since the time Luke introduced namespaces to R!},
`methods()` distinguishes in its returned object and the `print()` method of that between  hidden and visible methods, using the `*`
where the `*` is currently only used for namespace-only S3 methods.
I think we should

1. also use it (the `*`; or possibly other ascii markup) for hidden S4 methods {in `methods(qr)`}
2. also use it (some markup to distinguish hidden vs visible S4 methods) for `showMethods()`.

Unfortunately, `showMethods()` is currently a bit like a `print()` method but *without* the imporant print()-contract to return its input object invisibly.
I think we should really consider writing a `show()` {i.e., indirectly `print()`} method for `findMethods()` where that would need to be updated to return all methods from attached namespaces *and* distinguish which are currently dispatched from a call to `<generic>(...)`, in our example to methods seen from `qr()` {which is `base::qr`} and those seen from the `getGeneric("qr")`. Note the following -- nicely revealing and overlooked by me for the current problem:
```
> getGeneric("qr")
standardGeneric for "qr" defined from package "base"

function (x, ...) 
standardGeneric("qr")
<environment: 0x47478a88>
Methods may be defined for arguments: x
Use  showMethods(Matrix::qr)  for currently available ones.

> base::qr
function (x, ...) 
UseMethod("qr")
<bytecode: 0x3f8fb098>
<environment: namespace:base>
> 
```
Which is revealing on one hand but also "lying" to the useR  to some extent by starting to say
```
standardGeneric for "qr" defined from package "base"
```
(as when the user *does* look at `base::qr` that is *not* a standardGeneric ...).

All in all, I conclude the solution to this PR needs even more work,  but I definitely think I'd want this work be done
.. not at all necessarily by me or mostly me, though.
